title: A Minor Chord (Am) Tutorial: Fingering, Tuning Considerations, and Practice
summary: This JustinGuitar video teaches the A minor (Am) chord on guitar, starting from the A major fingering and showing how to transition to Am with a full finger change. It explains why Am can look like E major on a different set of strings, and why moving chord shapes down the neck is not a simple transposition due to guitar tuning—specifically, the B-string tuning pattern used in the 5th‑fret technique. The video pinpoints the key Am fingering (index on the 2nd string, middle and ring on the 4th and 3rd strings respectively) and notes that this same three-string layout is shared with A major. It also covers common alternative fingerings, cautions about muting issues (especially the open 5th string and the 2nd finger’s height), and closes with a practical practice method called “Chord Perfect Practice” that cycles through strumming and arpeggio picking to solidify correct fingering and future positions.

sections.description: The instructor covers the standard Am fingering (1-2-3) and notes occasional use of 2-3-4, with a caveat about distance and finger strength. A demonstration with the little finger shows how the Am shape can resemble A major, though it’s not recommended. The section also outlines common muting issues (especially with the 5th string and the 1st finger) and provides practical tips for precise finger placement and strain reduction. It concludes with the Chord Perfect Practice routine: strum, arpeggiate notes one by one, then strum again to reinforce the correct shape for future play.
